critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/domain/familyWeekly.ts:29 — grammar edge: 'has N alerts still open this week. A call to walk through it would help.' uses 'it' even when N>1 ('them' would read more naturally at 2+). Spec allows either 'is 1 or 2' so this is not a defect; consider ternary '${w.open_alerts > 1 ? "them" : "it"}' for polish.

/app/frontend/app/family.tsx:129 — weekly Pill labels for 'ears_up' → 'Handled' and 'neutral' → 'No news' are defined only in this file. If more weekly tones are added later, the mapping should probably move next to weeklyHeadline() to keep copy centralized.

/app/frontend/app/patrol/scent/[id].tsx:96–98 — incident-family-note-<i> label is rendered as one Text node followed by a timestamp Text and then the Call button; when read via textContent it concatenates as 'Sam: … ready.02:53 AMCall Sam back'. Visually spaced by RN flex, but same minor separator observation from iter-22 still applies (consider a '·' between note and timestamp for parity with family view).

/app/frontend/app/family/incident/[id].tsx:134 — family-note-phone is keyboard 'phone-pad', maxLength 32, sent as-is (server scrubs punctuation to digits/plus/spaces). Verified server returns '+61 4 11222 333' for '+61 (4) 11-222 333' — a bit unusual (spaces preserved without regrouping) but correct per backend test.
